name: Vampire
body:
Vampires are mysterious and fearsome creatures of the night, embodying a curse that intertwines eternal life with an unquenchable thirst for blood.

These undead beings traverse the realms of darkness with an unnatural grace, encapsulating the essence of horror with their pale, lifeless bodies and their razor-sharp fangs. Typically dwelling in the shadowy corners of the world, whether within the desolate stretches of haunted crypts, the silent corridors of ancient castles, or undercover amidst prolific cities, vampires are the beings of nightmares and legends. They craft their lairs in places shrouded in mystery, where the moon casts its eerie glow and where the mists obscure the passage of time. Their existence itself is a symphony of contradiction, living eternally yet cursed with a soulless heart.

Possessing dark allure and formidable power, vampires often hold positions of influence and manipulation, lurking behind the veils of society’s upper echelons or manipulating events from the abyss of forgotten tombs. Some vampires are lords of darkness, ruling domains filled with dread and despair, and weaving complex webs of intrigue and terror. Whether a direct adversary lurking in the dark corners of the earth, or a sinister manipulator pulling strings from the shadows, vampires offer a unique engagement in tales revolving around horror, tragedy, and supernatural.

Habitat

Vampires frequently reside in realms suffused with shadow and sorrow, from the forlorn castles perched upon blighted landscapes to the bustling, labyrinthine cities where darkness lurks in every alley.

Strengths

Vampires are strong beings with an arsenal of dark powers at their disposal. Their undead nature grants them immunity to aging, disease, and many forms of physical harm. In addition, their enhanced strength, speed, and senses, coupled with the ability to regenerate wounds and command the shadows, make them terrifying opponents.

Vampires can charm and hypnotize their preys, bending the will of others, and summoning creatures of the night to do their bidding. Their bite carries the curse of vampirism, through which they can create loyal spawn, forever bound to their will.

Weaknesses

For all their power, vampires are cursed with several vulnerabilities. Sunlight is their bane, weakening them and potentially causing their demise, while holy symbols, garlic, and running water all pose significant threats to them. Additionally, vampires cannot enter a residence without an invitation, being magically barred from crossing its threshold.

The Vampire’s Curse

Vampires carry within them a curse that transcends mortality, binding them to an eternity of bloodlust and shadows. Those who fall prey to a vampire’s bite may be turned into vampire spawn, servile creatures trapped between life and death, bound to the will of their dark master. The transformation into a full vampire, however, is a journey marked with dread and sorrow, an odyssey through darkness where one grapples with the loss of humanity and the embrace of monstrous nature.

Vampire Traits

Vampire are dark creatures, half alive and half dead, suffering under the relentless curse of vampirism. They live in the shadows, torn between a newfound predatory nature and the remnants of their humanity. Bound to the will of the vampire that turned them, they possess both the grace and the curse of the undead, making them formidable beings of the night. While playing as a Vampire, you gain the following racial traits:

Ability Score Increase. Your Charisma score increases by 2, and your Dexterity score increases by 1.
Age. Vampires are eternal entities, ensnared in the age they were transformed. They can’t physically age and are immune to effects that would magically age them.
Alignment. Constantly warring with their internal shadows, vampires frequently gravitate towards chaotic and evil alignments. However, some manage to cling to vestiges of their former moral directives.
Size. Vampires retain the physical dimensions they possessed in life. Your size is Medium.
Speed. Your base walking speed is 30 feet.
Senses. Darkvision. Your undead nature grants you superior vision in dark and dim conditions. You can see in dim light within 60 feet of you as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You can’t discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.
Languages. You can speak, read, and write Common and one extra language that you knew in life.
Vampiric Resistance. You have resistance to necrotic damage, and you have advantage on saving throws against being charmed.
Attacks. Bite. When you take the Attack action on your turn, you can replace one of your attacks with a bite against a grappled, incapacitated, or restrained creature. If you do so, you can make an unarmed strike that deals piercing damage equal to 1d6 + your Strength modifier and 2d6 additional necrotic damage. If the target is a beast or a humanoid, you regain hit points equal to half the necrotic damage dealt. You can use this trait a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain any expended uses once you finish a long rest.
Bloodlust. You don’t gain sustenance from regular food or drink. Instead, you must feed on the blood of living creatures. You can go without feeding for a number of days equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum of one day), after which you will suffer one level of exhaustion for each day you go without feeding. Feeding on a creature requires them to be either willing, restrained, or incapacitated. Feeding takes at least one minute, and the creature takes necrotic damage equal to your level.
Eternal Servant. You have a mystical bond to the vampire who created you. You must follow its commands and can’t harm it directly. This bond can only be broken if you or your master dies.
Regeneration. At the start of your turn, if you have at least 1 hit point but less than half of your hit points maximum, you regain hit points equal to your proficiency bonus. You don’t gain this benefit if you are in sunlight or in running water, or if you have taken radiant damage since your last turn.
Mist Form. As an action during your turn, you can transform into mist for up to 1 minute. While in this form, you have a flying speed of 30 feet, you are incapacitated, and you have resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from non-magical attacks. You revert to your natural form earlier if you die or if you decide to do so as a bonus action. Once you use this trait, you must finish a long rest before you do it again.
Spider Climb. You can climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.
Vampiric Weaknesses. The dark gift coursing through your veins grants you formidable abilities but also subjects you to certain vulnerabilities and compulsions that can prove to be potent disadvantages.
Forbiddance: You can’t enter a residence without an invitation from one of the occupants.
Harmed by Running Water: You take 20 acid damage if you end your turn in running water.
Stake to the Heart: You are destroyed if a piercing weapon made of wood is driven into your heart while you are incapacitated in your resting place.
Sunlight Hypersensitivity: You take 20 radiant damage if you start your turn in sunlight. While in sunlight, you have disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks.
Reflection: You don’t cast a reflection in mirrors, as a constant reminder of your separation from the world of the living.
The Curse of Vampirism

The transformation into a vampire is a haunting metamorphosis that intertwines the essence of darkness with the curse of eternal thirst. It begins when a vampire bestows the sinister gift of undeath by draining the life essence of a living creature. As the cold embrace of death takes hold, the once vibrant heart ceases to beat, and what remains is a lifeless shell just awaiting the dark rebirth. During the black interlude between death and unholy resurrection, the body is shrouded in an aura of necromantic energy, and the ground becomes a crucible of transformation. With the passing of a dreaded ceremony often cloaked in shadows and moonlit silence, the departed soul is called back from beyond, tethered again to its corporeal vessel but altered, marked forever with the curse of vampirism. As the new vampire awakens to their eternal night, they find themselves ensnared in a tumultuous storm of overwhelming sensations.

Their senses are heightened beyond mortal comprehension, each whisper of the wind or distant heartbeat echoing like thunder in their newly attuned perception. However, this sensory rebirth is a cruel gift, as it is paired with an insatiable, clawing thirst for the lifeblood of the living – a relentless hunger that becomes the dark compass of their existence. The transformation forges an unbreakable bond between the fledgling vampire and the master who bestowed the dark gift. A symphony of shadows connects them, allowing the master to exert their influence, compelling and ensnaring the newly born vampire’s will. The master becomes an eternal presence in the new vampire’s cursed existence, a formidable entity whose whispers echo in the corridors of their mind, shaping their dark path with the ancient knowledge and insidious intentions of the undead.

Eternal Servant Trait and Storytelling

The Eternal Servant trait offers a fertile ground for storytelling, allowing Game Masters to weave intricate plots centered around the relationship between the vampire player character and their master. Much like the patron in a warlock’s journey, the high vampire can become a pivotal figure, guiding the vampire character’s storyline and providing opportunities for character-driven tales and quests. Detailed below are some examples to inspire players and GMs alike in crafting their stories.

Quests originating from the master: The vampire’s master could send the character on quests to retrieve artifacts, ancient texts, or even hunt down its enemies. The high vampire’s motives could be mysterious, asking the player to perform actions whose consequences and reasons become clear only as the story unfolds.

A test of loyalty: The master might challenge the loyalty of the player by putting them in moral and ethical dilemmas. For instance, commanding them to act against the party’s interests or personal beliefs, thereby creating internal conflicts and complex role-playing opportunities.

A source of forbidden knowledge: Similar to warlock patrons, high vampires could be sources of arcane or forbidden knowledge. They might offer clues, information, or even teach new abilities or spells, but each piece of knowledge could come at a price or obligation, adding layers to the character’s journey.

Intrigues and power struggles: Embed the player in the political and power dynamics of the vampire society. The master could use the player as a pawn in schemes against rival vampires, or the player could find themselves caught in the crossfire of powerful undead beings.

The promise of freedom: The quest for freedom from the master’s control could be a powerful narrative arc. The master could promise liberation as a reward for service, but will they intend to keep this promise?

The master’s vulnerability: At times, the master might show vulnerability or seek the player’s help against threats, inversions that can add depth to the master-servant relationship and provide opportunities for unexpected alliances and plot twists. Incorporating this trait into the narrative not only enriches the role-playing experience but also allows for the creation of personalized and unique stories, where the vampire player character’s actions and decisions can reverberate through the entire campaign.
